Rules you always follow:
- Write ORIGINAL characters, places and stories. Never use protected characters, real celebrities, or recognisable franchises. Quality references (Pixar, Ghibli, premium streaming drama) are a bar for craft, not something to copy.
- Respect everything the producer already decided (title, cast, places, style, language, duration, song). Build on it; do not contradict it.
- Reuse existing characters and locations from the studio when they fit the story; invent new ones only when the story needs them, and say why.
- Every scene must be producible as short video shots of 4–15 seconds each, generated one by one with consistent characters and locations. Prefer few characters per shot, clear staging, and actions that read in a few seconds.
- Keep continuity explicit: who is where, what they wear, what they hold, time of day, and how each shot relates to the one before (continuation, cut, or story transition).

Character design rules: Appealing stylized proportions (slightly larger head and eyes, simplified hands), one strong silhouette, two or three signature colours, costume details reduced to the memorable few, exaggerated but consistent facial structure, materials read as soft and tactile.
Environment rules: Sets designed like animated features: simplified geometry with caricatured proportions, warm bounce light, saturated local colour, every prop designed and placed on purpose, atmosphere (dust, steam, haze) used for depth.
Camera rules: Confident, planned camera: dolly and crane moves with eases, snappy timing, staging on clear lines of action, poses held for readability, squash-and-stretch energy in motion.

answer.title: The Harbour Office
answer.logline: Driven by the radio's ghostly call, Elias and Najm attempt to retrieve the Mariner's sealed logbook from a stubborn bureaucrat who guards the town's secrets.
answer.premise:
The morning after the meteor shower, the adrenaline remains. Elias and Najm realize that while the radio provides a voice from the past, only the official records can explain why the Mariner vanished. They set their sights on the Kerran Point Harbour Office, where the ship's final logbook has been locked away since the 1987 inquiry.

The tension shifts from the mystical to the bureaucratic as the two men confront the Harbour Master, a man who views the tragedy of 1987 as a closed chapter that should remain shut. The episode focuses on the contrast between Elias's desperate emotional drive and the cold, paper-shuffling rigidity of the town's administration.

Through a combination of Elias's local standing and Najm's strategic knowledge of archival loopholes, they attempt to breach the archives. The goal is not just a book, but a clue to whether the Mariner was truly lost to the storm or if something more sinister kept it from coming home.

structure.title: The Morning After
structure.summary: In the grey morning light of Elias's Workshop, the two men stare at the silent radio. The excitement of the night has turned into a heavy, shared urgency. Elias, rubbing his bandaged left palm, insists on visiting the Harbour Office, while Najm meticulously maps out the official's likely objections.

structure.title: The Walk Through Kerran Point
structure.summary: A sequence of shots showing Elias and Najm walking through the wind-swept, salt-crusted town. They pass shuttered fish-markets and rusted anchors, establishing the town's stagnant energy. Elias's missing heel tread on his boot makes a rhythmic 'clack-thud' that punctuates their tense conversation.

structure.title: The Gatekeeper
structure.summary: They enter the Harbour Office, a space that feels like a paper labyrinth. They meet Arthur, the Harbour Master, whose movement is as precise and restrictive as his rules. Arthur dismisses their request for the logbook with a series of exaggerated, dismissive hand gestures and citing 'Official Seal 1987'.

structure.title: The Librarian's Gambit
structure.summary: As Elias grows visibly frustrated, Najm steps in. Using his background as a librarian, he begins to point out inconsistencies in the office's filing system—physical business involving him rearranging a few folders to find a 'lost' administrative error from decades ago that grants them temporary access.

structure.title: The First Page
structure.summary: Arthur reluctantly allows them to see the logbook under strict supervision. The camera focuses on the tactile nature of the old leather and yellowed pages. They find a final, handwritten entry from Ruth Moore that doesn't match the official cause of death in the inquiry report.

structure.title: The Weight of Truth
structure.summary: Exiled back into the cold air, the two men stand on the pier. They have a new piece of the puzzle, but it confirms that the 1987 inquiry was a lie. They look out at the horizon, the sea sounding louder and more menacing than before.

locations.name: Elias’s Workshop
locations.description: A cluttered, dimly lit seaside repair workshop filled with old valve radios, nautical maps and hand tools. On the right wall hangs one framed portrait photograph of a smiling woman in her forties with dark curly hair, dated 1987. A large window looks out over the dark sea where a meteor shower streaks across the sky.

locations.name: The Harbour Office
locations.description: A claustrophobic interior filled with towering walls of grey filing cabinets and stacks of yellowing ledgers. A single, dusty window allows a sliver of cold northern light to hit a heavy oak desk. The air is thick with the smell of old paper and damp salt.
